zoe (Docs): quick check before merge — PR #980 adds runnable snippets to the Optimize toolkit page. pavel called out two issues: the TypeScript example still uses `client.batch.send` (old) and the python streaming prefill example doesn't show the recommended prefetch call. also the quant comparison table reads too prescriptive for embeddings.
pavel (DevEx): dropping the exact snippets we landed so we can patch inline.
```ts
// current (stale) TS snippet in PR
const out = await client.batch.send({ items: [prompt], max_tokens: 128 })
console.log(out[0].text)
```
```py
# streaming prefill sample (incomplete)
stream = client.stream.start(model="redwood/fast-ggml", prompt=prompt)
for chunk in stream:
    print(chunk.text)
```
jihoon (Runtime): runtime/SDK note: `client.batch.send` is removed in v2; use `await client.batch.request({inputs: [...], max_tokens})` or `client.stream.open()` for streaming. also we renamed some cache helpers in SDK v2 — the correct call is `client.cache.prefetch(prefixes)` (not prefill). For streaming with repeated short prefixes, call `client.cache.prefetch([...])` before opening the stream to save KV recompute. add a short caveat: prefetching many unique prefixes increases memory.
anya (ML): on quant: please avoid absolutist language. suggest: "q8_0: cost-efficient; run a 1k-sample embedding drift check and a 200-sample generation fidelity check before switching." add a tiny micro-eval snippet that seeds RNGs for reproducibility.
pavel (DevEx): here's the minimal fix i'm testing now — replacement TS + python prefetch snippet:
```ts
// replacement TS
const resp = await client.batch.request({ inputs: [prompt], max_tokens: 128 })
console.log(resp[0].text)
```
```py
# add prefetch before streaming
client.cache.prefetch(["session_prefix_v4"])  # avoid repeated KV work
stream = client.stream.open(model="redwood/fast-ggml", prompt=prompt)
for chunk in stream.recv():
    print(chunk.get_text())
```
